messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV_CACHE continuous-batching eviction rate spike detected on prod-serving cluster us-east-1a. Evictions: 52/s -> 980/s, tail-latency > 1200ms, paging events observed. Auto-escalation to #incidents and paging cycle started.

sam: oncall, I'm seeing the same in datadog. paging eng-runtime + eng-oncall. tagging maya and liam.

maya: I’m on the pager. first cut: reduce batch window and throttle continuous-batching for high-throughput tenants.

liam: agreed. hypothesis = batch_window + long prefix reuse causing KV cache amplification -> eviction + paging. prepping feature-flag hotfix.

sofia: any customer-facing impact? telemetry shows error-rate uptick for high-QPS tenants, some 5xx spikes tied to KV timeouts.

jordan: acme-pay and delta-bank show the biggest tail-latency and token-timeouts. acme-pay is 18% of requests on affected nodes.

maya: immediate plan: 1) roll canary change to reduce default batch_window_ms from 1000 -> 200 for 5% of traffic. 2) apply per-customer override (acme-pay, delta-bank, beta-retail) to 150ms. 3) enable fallback routing to small-model variant for tenants that hit >500ms tail.

liam: config prepared. will use the feature-flag service. command:
```bash
# set canary to 5% for continuous-batching throttle
curl -X POST https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/continuous_batch_window/rollout -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" -d '{\"percentage\":5,\"value_ms\":200}'
```

liam: per-tenant override example (acme-pay):
```bash
curl -X PUT https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/tenants/acme-pay/flags -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" -d '{\"continuous_batch_window_ms\":150}'
```

sam: Maya, can you coordinate the per-tenant ops? Liam, run the canary now and watch eviction rate and 5xx. I'll open a short rota for infra to check IO on the nodes.

maya: starting per-tenant overrides for acme-pay -> delta-bank -> beta-retail in that order. executing now.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for flag-change-job #7821. CI checks pass. Canary rollout scheduled.

liam: canary started at 2223456920. monitoring feed: metrics histograms hooked into #incidents-monitoring.

sam: quick queries I ran:
```
# datadog query snippet
avg:kvcache.evictions{env:prod,cluster:us-east-1a}.rollup(sum,60) by {tenant}
```
shows acme-pay jumping at the same timestamp as client retries.

sofia: acme-pay support pinged SRE; they see degraded response times in logs and some request retries. no PII.

jordan: notifying account lead for acme-pay. they're expecting us to throttle gracefully.

liam: canary results after 4 minutes: eviction rate for canary hosts dropped ~60%, tail-latency down ~40% on canary slices, no increase in 5xx. moving to 25% rollout.

maya: rolling per-customer overrides complete for acme-pay and delta-bank. beta-retail on deck.

sam: good. increase to 25% now. monitor 10m windows and paged dashboards.

liam: 25% -> metrics stable. no paging on canary hosts. executing global roll from 25% -> 100% in staged batches (25% steps).

ops-bot: global rollout stage 1 -> 25% done. stage 2 -> 50% started.

sofia: customer impact update: acme-pay error-rate back to normal range, delta-bank improving, beta-retail had a transient spike during override but settled. no escalations from customers right now.

jordan: note for post-incident: need a per-tenant load classification and automatic per-tenant flags when eviction > threshold. capturing runbook gaps.

liam: final rollout to 100% completed at 2223456898. verified eviction rates across cluster returned to baseline. paging events cleared.

sam: nice work. immediate mitigation = feature-flag batch_window reduction + per-tenant overrides. follow-ups: 1) postmortem (owner: jordan) 2) add guardrail to auto-scale KV mem reserve 3) investigate root cause of traffic patterns that amplified batch reuse.

maya: handing off monitoring to sofia for next 2 hours. sofia, ping me if anything regresses.

sofia: taking over monitoring. will notify at 09:00 UTC for shift change.

jordan: I’ll own the postmortem, will draft and link to this thread. tagging @product and @sre for follow-up on long-term mitigations.

sam: closing incident channel when we have 2h stable. adding incident label and scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
